agent.problem: Stop 2, card 10 quotes "Let this be written for the generation to come.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

agent.problem: The first two answers offer possible meanings of the smoke picture, but “His home is burning down” abruptly switches to a literal, silly event. It is not a believable answer to what the man is saying about his life and makes the right answer stand out.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

agent.problem: The question says the man “calls himself a desert owl” and the other birds, changing the text's comparisons into direct self-descriptions. Verses 6-7 say he is like these birds.
Card 5 has already told the baker that the man's heart is “withered like grass,” giving away “grass” as the answer to this later blank.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

agent.problem: Nothing in the earlier cards introduces clothing or another image for wearing out. The baker must guess which word completes an unseen line rather than reason about the passage's movement or meaning.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

agent.problem: The statement that God “outlasts the HEAVENS” uses verse 26's statement that the heavens will perish as well as verse 27's statement that God remains. Citing only verse 27 is too narrow; the card uses verses 26-27.

rule.text: Cite exactly what the card uses. Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

human.problem: All six true or false cards in the walkthrough (stop 1 cards 2, 10 and 13; stop 2 cards 4, 8 and 20) have False as the right answer. A baker could learn to always pick False. The code shuffles answer position, but that doesn't help with true or false.
human.question: Should there be a rule that true or false cards mix True and False right answers, so bakers can't learn a pattern?
